idiom_name: concept unit (class, aggregate or module) + narrow domain interface
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: for each domain concept choose one unit that owns its state, invariants and operations, expose only operations that make sense in the ubiquitous language, and keep the representation hidden (private fields, unexported names, module-private functions). Move behaviour to the unit that has the data it needs instead of letting clients or external services reach in; when an operation genuinely spans concepts, put it in an explicit coordinating unit (a domain service) rather than dissolving both concepts. Re-cut the units as the model deepens, because a contour is a hypothesis about the domain that successive refactorings confirm or falsify.
code_sketch:
# the contour is the unit, not the file
unit Invoice
  state:     lines, currency          (hidden)
  invariant: lines share currency; status transitions are legal
  api:       add_line(line), pay(), total
  not api:   set_status(status), internal_buffer

client:  invoice.add_line(line); invoice.pay()
never:   invoice.set_status('paid')   # client reaches into the concept
pitfalls: Treating the file, layer or service as the contour: units cut by technical convenience re-scatter the concept.
Exposing the representation because a framework or caller wants it; every getter widened for convenience erodes the interface.
Assuming one shape of contour fits all concepts: grain and axes of change differ between concepts in the same model.
Preferring deep inheritance hierarchies over flat concept units: inheritance crosses contour boundaries and tightens coupling.
Allowing domain services to accumulate logic that belongs on a concept: a domain service should coordinate, not replace.
